title: The 3D grid
caption: Every layout is a point in the parallelism cube: data-parallel replicas times pipeline stages times tensor-parallel shards. The reference job sits at 16 x 8 x 8 = 1,024; the 16K layout at 128 x 16 x 8 = 16,384. A legal point must divide the model evenly, fit each device's memory, and put each axis's traffic on a fabric tier that can carry it.

symbols.meaning: total accelerators in the cluster
data-parallel degree: replicas, the batch axis
pipeline-parallel degree: layer stages, the depth axis
tensor-parallel degree: intra-layer shards, usually one node

title: The training-state contract
caption: Mixed-precision Adam prices 16 bytes per parameter: 2-byte BF16 weights, 2-byte gradients, and a 12-byte optimizer (FP32 master plus two moments). On the 175B reference that is 2.8 TB of state against 80 GB of HBM, at least 35 accelerators of capacity before a single FLOP.

symbols.meaning: parameter count
bytes per parameter under mixed-precision Adam (2 + 2 + 12)
the 175B reference job's resumable training state

title: Scaling efficiency
caption: Amdahl's law with communication: every worker's exposed communication, synchronization, and straggler time is scaled by N against one device's compute. A 1 percent residual per worker is ~84 percent of the step at 512. The reference job lands eta = 83 percent; measured series sit at 71-84 percent at the largest sizes.

symbols.meaning: scaling efficiency: useful-compute fraction of the step
per-worker communication time
synchronization and barrier wait
communication hidden under compute
per-device useful compute time

title: The pipeline bubble
caption: Of the m + p - 1 slots in a pipeline schedule, p - 1 are idle while the pipe fills and drains. PP-16 at 32 microbatches idles ~32 percent of compute; the same microbatch count at PP-4 wastes ~9 percent. Depth buys memory relief at the price of idle compute, and filling the pipe needs more microbatches, which pushes on the critical batch size.

symbols.meaning: pipeline stage count
microbatches per update per replica
stages that must fill before full occupancy

title: Critical batch size
caption: The gradient-noise estimate of where batch scaling stops paying: the trace of the gradient covariance over the squared gradient norm. Below B*, larger batches cut optimization steps nearly proportionally; above it, extra samples buy diminishing reductions. It is a statistical ceiling on data parallelism, separate from the memory-limited batch.

symbols.meaning: critical batch size, the diminishing-returns crossover
total gradient noise: trace of the gradient covariance
squared gradient norm, the signal the batch averages toward

title: Activation memory scaling
latex: M_{act} = \mathcal{O}(B \cdot S \cdot H \cdot L) \quad\text{linear layers};\qquad \mathcal{O}(B \cdot A \cdot S^{2} \cdot L) \quad\text{un-tiled attention}
caption: At long contexts the activations, not the weights, are the footprint: linear in sequence length for ordinary layers, quadratic for un-tiled attention. FlashAttention drops the stored score matrix but not the linear growth. GPT-3's unoptimized activations exceed 1 TB at batch 4, sequence 2048; full checkpointing fits them under 25 GB, trading recompute for memory.

symbols.meaning: batch, sequence length, hidden width, layer count
attention head count
